content.title: King Charles and Queen Camilla Are “the Most Compatible Royal Couple,” as She Brings Out This “Rarely” Seen Side of Him
content.text: King Charles and Queen Camilla on February 23, 2023Credit: GettyThe GistKing Charles and Queen Camilla are celebrating 21 years of marriage on April 9.Though they’ve been married since 2005, their love story really began—and likely never stopped—after meeting in 1970, 56 years ago.“I would say Charles and Camilla are the most compatible royal couple,” body language expert Darren Stanton tells InStyle.April 9 marks King Charles and Queen Camilla’s 21st wedding anniversary, and their body language proves that they are “the most compatible royal couple,” according to an expert.Speaking to InStyle, body language expert Darren Stanton says that the couple—who met in 1970 and have held affection for one another ever since—still exhibit the “same passion” from when they first met 56 years ago.King Charles and Queen Camilla at Royal Ascot on June 20, 2024Credit: Getty“I would say Charles and Camilla are the most compatible royal couple,” Stanton says. “They have had this deep love since they were both very young. We’re talking about a 50-year-plus romance. They’ve been in love a long time, and it’s been an intense relationship where they’ve had to overcome a lot.”This included both marrying other people—Camilla married Andrew Parker Bowles in 1973, and they share two children, Tom Parker Bowles and Laura Lopes; Charles married Lady Diana Spencer in 1981, and they share Prince William and Prince Harry. Both marriages ended in divorce in the 1990s, and Charles and Camilla married in 2005.Prince Charles and Camilla Parker Bowles on their April 9, 2005 wedding dayCredit: Getty“Even looking at pictures of them when they were younger, whenever Camilla was photographed, it’s so clear they had this deep intensity for one another, and it has continued to grow,” Stanton says on behalf of Betfair Casino. “They have the same passion for each other still to this day.”Stanton adds, “During public events, Charles is often looking around and fidgeting when Camilla isn’t by his side, which shows how dependent he is on her. But when they are together, we see this genuine laughter shared between them with engaged eye contact, and this shows how they are on the same page emotionally. When he was a young prince, we rarely saw him display a relaxed nature. Camilla brings that side out of him where he can be himself, let go, and just enjoy his time as king.”When Charles and Camilla married in 2005, they did so in a civil ceremony at Windsor Guildhall in front of just 28 guests—and that number did not include Charles’s parents, Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip. As head of the Church of England, the Queen decided that it wasn’t appropriate for her to be at the wedding of two people who had divorced their first spouses, per People. That said, the Queen and the Duke of Edinburgh did attend a Service of Prayer and Dedication at St. George’s Chapel on the grounds of Windsor Castle after the ceremony, and they also held a reception for the newlyweds.Prince Charles and Camilla Parker Bowles on their wedding dayCredit: GettyUnlike many royal brides, Camilla eschewed wearing a tiara. For her wedding ceremony, Camilla wore a wide-brimmed, feather-accented hat by Philip Treacy, along with a white silk chiffon dress and matching coat. She then changed into a floor-length embroidered blue and gold coat over a blue chiffon gown, People reported, this time accessorizing with a gold feather headpiece, also by Treacy.Camilla’s longtime hairstylist Jo Hansford told Hello! in 2025 that Camilla was “so nervous” on her wedding day, but added, “She looked amazing, thank God.”“The whole world was watching, and it must have been terrifying, the same as the [2023] coronation,” Hansford added. “But I think she handled it really well.” She continued, “I admire them both. I think the King is amazing—he is definitely his mother’s son. He’s a stalwart—absolutely incredible. I think she supports him incredibly well, and I think he’s very lucky.”“It’s just a shame they didn’t do it before, but the most important thing is that they’re happy together and they’re both right for each other,” Hansford said.Prince Charles and Camilla Parker Bowles on April 9, 2005Credit: GettyVeteran royal photographer Arthur Edwards told People that Camilla makes Charles “laugh,” he said. “When something triggers them, you see them just laughing together. They do things with such enthusiasm.”“She calmed him down,” Edwards said. “She’s got an amazing way to soothe him.”Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall and Prince Charles on August 6, 2005Credit: GettyRoyal biographer Christopher Wilson added that Charles and Camilla “work well as a team. It’s impressive. Her presence reassures him. Despite all the trappings of majesty, it’s cold and lonely at the top, and it’s easy to see the comfort she provides him.”A close palace source told People that “She is the yin to his yang. She is the type to say, ‘It’ll all be fine—let’s crack on and get on with things.’”Read the original article on InStyle
